name: International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO)
subject: Mathematics
blurb: The most prestigious pre-college math contest. Even a national-round result is a serious signal.

name: International Physics Olympiad (IPhO)
subject: Physics
blurb: Elite physics olympiad. National-level qualification already reads as exceptional for STEM admits.

name: International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI)
subject: Programming / Algorithms
blurb: Premier competitive-programming olympiad. Gold-standard evidence of algorithmic ability for CS.

name: USACO (USA Computing Olympiad)
subject: Competitive Programming
blurb: Open to anyone worldwide and fully online. Reaching Gold/Platinum is a concrete, verifiable CS spike.

name: International Biology Olympiad (IBO)
subject: Biology
blurb: Strong signal for pre-med and life-sciences applicants. Start from your national biology olympiad.

name: International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO)
subject: Chemistry
blurb: Theory + lab chemistry at the highest level. National qualification is a major differentiator.

name: Regeneron ISEF
subject: Any STEM research
deadline_label: Finals — qualify via local fairs earlier
blurb: The world’s largest pre-college science fair. A finalist project is one of the strongest STEM credentials available.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
subject: STEM research (summer)
blurb: Free, ultra-selective summer research program at MIT. One of the most respected lines on any STEM application.

name: Pioneer Research Program
subject: Mentored research (any field)
blurb: Online 1-on-1 research with a university professor, ending in a paper. Open to most fields, including humanities.

name: Diamond Challenge
subject: Entrepreneurship
blurb: Global high-school entrepreneurship competition. Great for turning a club or side project into a credential.

name: International Economics Olympiad (IEO)
subject: Economics / Finance
blurb: Economics, finance and business-case rounds. Ideal spike for prospective economics/business majors.

name: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
subject: Investing / Finance
blurb: Run by UPenn’s Wharton School. Teams manage a virtual portfolio and pitch a strategy — strong for finance interest.

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
subject: Writing / Visual Art
blurb: The most recognised US creative award for teens. A National Medal is meaningful for humanities/arts applicants.

name: JFK Profile in Courage Essay Contest
subject: Essay / Political Science
blurb: National essay contest with cash prizes. Good for demonstrating writing and civic/political interest.

name: John Locke Institute Essay Competition
subject: Philosophy / Economics / History
blurb: Rigorous open-ended essays judged by Oxford-affiliated academics. Highly regarded for humanities/social-science applicants.

name: World Schools Debating Championships
subject: Debate / Public Speaking
blurb: Top-tier debate. Even strong national-circuit results demonstrate argument, research and leadership.

name: Model United Nations (e.g. HMUN, THIMUN)
subject: Diplomacy / Policy
blurb: Accessible entry point for leadership and global affairs. Awards at flagship conferences (HMUN) carry weight.

name: Launch your own initiative / nonprofit
subject: Self-directed impact
blurb: Not a contest — a self-started project solving a real problem in your community. Measurable impact often beats a generic award.

name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
subject: Leadership / All-round
blurb: Prestigious US leadership scholarship ($20k). Recognition itself is a strong line, beyond the money.

name: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS)
subject: Interdisciplinary
blurb: Two-week academic summer program at Yale with strong financial aid. Good for exploring interests and intl exposure.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition
subject: Robotics / Engineering
blurb: Teams build a competition robot in six weeks. Tangible engineering + leadership signal, and a feeder for awards and scholarships.

name: Hackathons (MLH-affiliated)
subject: Software / Building
blurb: Build a working project in 24–48 hours, solo or in a team. Low barrier, fully remote, and a great source of portfolio projects.

name: International Linguistics Olympiad (IOL)
subject: Linguistics / Logic
blurb: Logic puzzles over real languages — no prior linguistics needed. A distinctive spike for CS, languages and cognitive science.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
subject: Science communication
blurb: Explain a tough science concept in a short video. Accessible worldwide, with a large scholarship and real prestige.

name: Conrad Challenge
subject: Innovation / Entrepreneurship
blurb: Teams design a product or venture tackling a real-world problem. A good bridge between STEM and entrepreneurship.

name: DECA / FBLA (business clubs)
subject: Business / Marketing / Finance
blurb: Case and role-play business competitions with a clear regional→state→international ladder. Accessible and well-recognised for business majors.

name: National History Day
subject: History / Research
blurb: Year-long historical research presented as a paper, exhibit, documentary or performance. A strong humanities research credential.

name: GENIUS Olympiad
subject: Environmental projects (STEM/arts/writing)
blurb: Environment-themed projects across science, art, writing and design. A broad entry point for an issue-driven applicant.

name: AMC 10/12 → AIME
subject: Mathematics
blurb: The on-ramp to the US math-olympiad pipeline. Qualifying for AIME is a recognised, verifiable math credential.

name: Harvard–MIT Math Tournament (HMMT)
subject: Mathematics
blurb: One of the largest and most prestigious student-run math competitions, hosted by Harvard and MIT.

name: Math Kangaroo
subject: Mathematics
blurb: Accessible global math contest across all grade levels — a good first competitive math experience.

name: European Girls’ Math Olympiad (EGMO)
subject: Mathematics
blurb: Premier international math olympiad for girls; national selection mirrors the IMO pipeline.

name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
subject: Biology
blurb: The US route toward the IBO. Semifinalist/finalist standing is a strong signal for bio and pre-med.

name: F=ma / USA Physics Olympiad
subject: Physics
blurb: The F=ma exam feeds USAPhO and the US physics team. Top scores are elite physics credentials.

name: US National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO)
subject: Chemistry
blurb: National chemistry exam and camp selection on the route to the IChO.

name: International Brain Bee
subject: Neuroscience
blurb: Neuroscience competition for teens — distinctive for prospective bio/medicine and psychology applicants.

name: iGEM (Synthetic Biology)
subject: Synthetic Biology
blurb: Build a real synthetic-biology project as a team and present at the global jamboree. Serious lab/research signal.

name: Int’l Olympiad on Astronomy & Astrophysics
subject: Astronomy / Astrophysics
blurb: Top astronomy olympiad combining theory, data analysis and observation.

name: Meta Hacker Cup
subject: Competitive Programming
blurb: Global online algorithmic contest run by Meta — open to anyone and fully remote.

name: Congressional App Challenge
subject: App Development
blurb: Build an app and win recognition from your US representative — accessible entry into CS credentials.

name: Technovation Girls
subject: App / Entrepreneurship
blurb: Girls build a mobile app to solve a community problem, with mentorship and a global pitch.

name: Codeforces (rated contests)
subject: Competitive Programming
blurb: The main global platform for competitive programming. A strong rating is concrete, continuous evidence of skill.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
subject: Original STEM research
blurb: The oldest and most prestigious US science research competition. Finalist status is exceptional.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
subject: Significant project (STEM/arts)
blurb: Up to $50k for a genuinely significant piece of work. A top-tier credential for a deep project.

name: Junior Science & Humanities Symposium
subject: STEM research
blurb: Present original research at a regional symposium with scholarships and a path to nationals.

name: MIT THINK Scholars
subject: STEM project proposal
blurb: Pitch a STEM project you want to build; finalists get funding and MIT mentorship. Great for makers.

name: DECA
subject: Business / Marketing
blurb: Large business case + role-play competition with a clear path from local to international finals.

name: FBLA (Future Business Leaders)
subject: Business
blurb: Accessible business competition spanning dozens of events — good for demonstrating business interest.

name: National Economics Challenge
subject: Economics
blurb: The premier US high-school economics competition — strong for prospective econ majors.

name: Blue Ocean Entrepreneurship Competition
subject: Entrepreneurship
blurb: Free, fully online startup pitch competition — low barrier, real prize money and recognition.

name: The Concord Review
subject: History essays
blurb: The only journal publishing high-school history research papers — a serious credential for humanities.

name: New York Times Student Contests
subject: Writing / Multimedia
blurb: A rotating series of free writing, editorial and multimedia contests with wide recognition.

name: Bow Seat Ocean Awareness Contest
subject: Art / Writing / Film
blurb: Creative contest on environmental themes — accessible and good for art/writing portfolios with a cause.

name: YoungArts
subject: Visual / Performing / Literary Arts
blurb: The most prestigious US arts recognition for teens; winners join a notable alumni network.

name: NSDA Speech & Debate Nationals
subject: Debate / Speech
blurb: The flagship US speech and debate circuit; deep results show argument, research and poise.

name: Congressional Award (Gold Medal)
subject: Service / Self-development
blurb: Congress’s award for young people: log service, personal development and a journey. Self-driven and respected.

name: Rise (Schmidt Futures × Rhodes Trust)
subject: Talent / Service
blurb: A global fellowship for 15–17-year-olds with lifetime benefits. Among the most prestigious programs available.

name: LaunchX
subject: Entrepreneurship
blurb: Intensive summer program where students launch a real startup. Strong for entrepreneurial spikes.

name: MIT MITES (Summer)
subject: STEM
blurb: Free, rigorous MIT STEM program for high-achieving students from underrepresented backgrounds.

name: Stanford University Math Camp (SUMaC)
subject: Mathematics
blurb: Deep abstract-math summer program at Stanford — strong for prospective math/CS students.

name: PROMYS
subject: Number Theory / Math
blurb: Intensive proof-based number theory at Boston University. Beloved by serious young mathematicians.

name: Ross Mathematics Program
subject: Number Theory / Math
blurb: Classic “think deeply about simple things” math immersion — a hallmark for aspiring mathematicians.

name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
subject: Astrophysics / Biochem / Genomics
blurb: Residential research program where teams complete a real scientific project — excellent research signal.

name: COSMOS (UC)
subject: STEM
blurb: University of California STEM summer immersion across many clusters — solid exploratory program.

name: USA Math Talent Search (USAMTS)
subject: Mathematics
blurb: Free, proof-based, month-long take-home math contest — rewards depth over speed and needs no travel.

name: MATHCOUNTS
subject: Mathematics
blurb: The premier US middle-school math competition and a strong early foundation for the olympiad pipeline.

name: Purple Comet Math Meet
subject: Mathematics
blurb: Free international team math contest run entirely online — accessible, collaborative and genuinely fun.

name: Science Olympiad
subject: Multi-discipline STEM
blurb: 23-event team science tournament spanning biology, chemistry, physics and engineering builds.

name: DOE National Science Bowl
subject: Science & Math
blurb: Fast-paced quiz-style science and math tournament run by the US Department of Energy.

name: Physics Bowl (AAPT)
subject: Physics
blurb: A timed AAPT physics exam open worldwide — a low-barrier way to benchmark physics ability.

name: Int’l Earth Science Olympiad (IESO)
subject: Earth & Space Science
blurb: The top pre-college olympiad for geology, meteorology, oceanography and astronomy.

name: Int’l Junior Science Olympiad (IJSO)
subject: General Science
blurb: Multidisciplinary science olympiad for younger students — an early elite STEM credential.

name: Kaggle Competitions
subject: Data Science / ML
blurb: The global platform for data-science and ML competitions. Medals and tier ranks are verifiable credentials.

name: picoCTF (Carnegie Mellon)
subject: Cybersecurity
blurb: Carnegie Mellon’s beginner-friendly cybersecurity capture-the-flag — free, online and hugely popular.

name: CyberPatriot
subject: Cyber Defense
blurb: The US national youth cyber-defense competition — a strong signal for security-minded CS applicants.

name: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute
subject: AI / Engineering
blurb: Free, rigorous MIT project-based AI and engineering institute — an outstanding maker credential.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC)
subject: Robotics / Engineering
blurb: Varsity-scale robotics: design, build and field a large robot in six weeks. Deep teamwork and engineering.

name: VEX Robotics World Championship
subject: Robotics / Engineering
blurb: One of the largest robotics competitions globally, with a clear path from local events to Worlds.

name: Stanford SIMR
subject: Biomedical Research
blurb: Paid biomedical research internship at Stanford — a top-tier wet-lab research experience.

name: Simons Summer Research Program
subject: University Research
blurb: Stony Brook program placing students in real university labs with a stipend, a mentor and a final poster.

name: Garcia Summer Research (Stony Brook)
subject: Materials Science
blurb: Polymer and materials-science research immersion — many participants co-author papers or patents.

name: Clark Scholar Program (Texas Tech)
subject: Any Field Research
blurb: Seven-week one-on-one research program with a stipend — extremely selective and open to all fields.

name: Perimeter ISSYP (Physics)
subject: Theoretical Physics
blurb: Perimeter Institute’s theoretical-physics program for teens — free and globally competitive.

name: TASP / TASS (Telluride)
subject: Humanities Seminar
blurb: Free, discussion-based humanities seminar — among the most prestigious programs for writers and thinkers.

name: Wharton M&TSI (Penn)
subject: Business + Engineering
blurb: Penn’s Management & Technology Summer Institute — engineering plus business for future founders.

name: Girls Who Code Summer Program
subject: Computer Science
blurb: Free virtual CS program teaching real coding and community — a strong, accessible entry into tech.

name: Kode With Klossy
subject: Computer Science
blurb: Free coding camps in web, ML and mobile — a supportive on-ramp for underrepresented students in tech.

name: Bank of America Student Leaders
subject: Civic Leadership
blurb: A paid summer internship at a nonprofit plus a national leadership summit in Washington, DC.

name: NFTE World Series of Innovation
subject: Entrepreneurship
blurb: Design a business solution to a global challenge — free, online and beginner-friendly entrepreneurship.

name: Prudential Emerging Visionaries
subject: Social / Financial Impact
blurb: Awards for young people driving financial or societal change in their communities.

name: World Scholar’s Cup
subject: Debate / Writing / Quiz
blurb: A global team academic tournament (debate, writing, quiz) with a famously welcoming community.

name: USA Academic Decathlon
subject: Multi-subject
blurb: A ten-event team academic competition around a yearly theme — rewards breadth and teamwork.

name: Quiz Bowl (NAQT)
subject: General Knowledge
blurb: Fast-recall academic buzzer competition spanning every subject — a classic team credential.

name: National Latin Exam
subject: Latin / Classics
blurb: A global Latin exam with awards at each level — a distinctive classics credential.

name: The Adroit Prizes
subject: Poetry & Prose
blurb: Prestigious poetry and prose prizes for students, judged by acclaimed contemporary writers.

name: Foyle Young Poets of the Year
subject: Poetry
blurb: One of the world’s biggest youth poetry awards, run by the UK Poetry Society. Free to enter.

name: QuestBridge National College Match
subject: Full Scholarship
blurb: Matches outstanding low-income US students with full four-year scholarships to top partner colleges.

name: The Gates Scholarship
subject: Full Scholarship
blurb: A full ride for exceptional minority students with financial need — extremely selective.

name: Jack Kent Cooke Young Scholars
subject: Need-based Support
blurb: Multi-year funding and mentorship for high-achieving students with financial need, starting in 8th grade.

name: International Zhautykov Olympiad (IZhO)
subject: Mathematics, Physics, Informatics
blurb: Annual international olympiad in Almaty run by the Republican Physics and Mathematics School — a well-known credential for students in math, physics and informatics.
